source_document: data/ISO_IEC_TR_30172_2023(en)_Internet of things (loT) - Digital twin - Use cases.pdf (ISO/IEC TR 30172:2023(en), Internet of Things (IoT) - Digital twin - Use cases)
role_in_kg: digital_twin_use_case_evidence: the published evidence base that digital twins of the kind this repo's PdM/CDT use case builds are being deployed - fourteen collected use cases incl. an engineering-and-maintenance rail twin (B.11) whose scope literally layers asset data, fault notifications and work orders over a point-cloud foundation. Also supplies the DT quality vocabulary (conformity, reliability, fidelity, robustness, traceability) - conformity (3.6) being the vocabulary-level description of the CDT-readiness audit verdict.

extraction_notes.registry_scope: Reconciliation registry is the union of the twelve preceding extraction files. Nine of the fifteen clause-3 terms are reused from ISO/IEC 30173 or earlier files (digital twin, entity, physical entity, digital entity - 30172 3.4 says 'computational element' where 30173 3.1.5 says 'computational entitiy', same concept - life cycle, verification, validation, synchronization, interoperability). Six are new: conformity (digital twin) - a deliberate qualified fork against ISO 55000's conformity, different referent, joined by CORRESPONDS_TO - reliability, robustness, fidelity, traceability, reconfigurability.
extraction_notes.id_convention: Keeps term_<snake_case>; adds usecase_<snake_case> for the fourteen Annex B collected use cases, in the same spirit as the existing specialized prefixes. Use case definitions are their verbatim Annex B headings (the P2/P3 heading-chain precedent); names equal the headings.
extraction_notes.verbatim_convention: All definitions are verbatim ISO/IEC TR 30172:2023 text (segments joined by ' [...] '), asserted at build time and enforced by backend/gates/verify_verbatim.py. Two text-layer artifacts quoted as extracted: 'welldefined' (3.11, line-break hyphen dropped by pdftotext). The use case template node quotes the Annex A heading chain.
extraction_notes.structure_notes: The fourteen Annex B use case narratives (8-15 pages each, with figures) are represented as one node each: verbatim heading as definition, PdM-relevant verbatim quotes in notes (B.11 objectives and scope), and targeted edges to existing graph concepts. Clause 6 statistics and Annex B diagrams are not nodeified.
extraction_notes.bsdd_mapping: Checked against the buildingSMART Data Dictionary (2026-08-05): no genuine matches for DT quality vocabulary. Absence means checked-no-genuine-match.
extraction_notes.merge_note: File name does not match the iso19650-* union glob; it is listed explicitly in the union tooling and must always be loaded together with the other twelve files.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: conformity (digital twin)
nodes.definition: process of analysis to determine whether a digital twin meets the specified requirements and to form a judgement as to whether the digital entity is fit for its corresponding physical entity
nodes.note: Distinct referent from ISO 55000:2024 3.3.17 conformity (fulfilment of a requirement): here it is the DT-specific fitness-judgement process. This is the vocabulary-level description of the CDT-readiness audit in this repo - the CDT-READY / NOT-READY verdict is a conformity judgement on whether the digital entity (IFC-seeded twin) is fit for its physical asset.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: reliability
nodes.definition: ability of an item to perform a required function under given conditions for a given time interval
nodes.note: [SOURCE: IEC 62657-1:2017, 3.1.12, modified.] The quantity predictive maintenance protects: RUL prediction and condition monitoring exist to keep this ability above target.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: robustness
nodes.definition: degree to which a system or component can function correctly in the presence of invalid inputs or stressful environmental conditions
nodes.note: [SOURCE: ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765:2017, 3.3555].

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: fidelity
nodes.definition: ability to accurately describe the relevant aspects of the physical counterpart within a welldefined set of conditions by its digital model
nodes.note: The source text hyphenates 'well-defined' across a line break, rendered as 'welldefined' in the text layer - quoted as extracted.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: traceability
nodes.definition: ability to trace the history, application or location of an object
nodes.note: [SOURCE: ISO 9000:2015, 3.6.13, modified.]

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: reconfigurability
nodes.definition: ability of an artefact to be changed through configuration changes rather than having to modify its underlying structure or its code or both

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: digital twin application domain
nodes.definition: DTw application domains can be classified into industry-based categories, and specific use cases can serve as examples for each category.
nodes.note: Domains listed for use-case collection include building or construction, manufacturing, energy, transport and cities; 5.2 records life cycle stage coverage; 6.3 gives basic statistics of the collected use cases by domain and life cycle status.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: digital twin use case template
nodes.definition: Use case template [...] Description of use case [...] Drawings or diagrams depicting the use case
nodes.note: Template fields A.2.1-A.2.19: name; application area or context; version management; basic information; scope; objectives; narrative; entities to be modelled as digital entities; actors (people, organizations or systems); life cycle of the digital twin system; key performance indicators (KPIs); digital infrastructures; referenced standards and committees; referenced papers or patents; relations with other use cases; general remarks; challenges and issues; data security, privacy and trustworthiness; user requirements and interactions. A.3: use case drawing plus optional data flow, sequence and deployment diagrams. A structured intake form for specifying a digital twin use case - directly reusable for specifying the PdM/CDT use case.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: Transport - Sydney Trains Engineering and Maintenance Digital Twin
nodes.definition: Transport - Sydney Trains Engineering and Maintenance Digital Twin
nodes.note: Objectives (verbatim): 'To provide asset managers, planners, engineers and infrastructure workers with a holistic, self-selecting, filterable view of all elements of planning and executing work in the rail corridor to reduce safety risks and to optimize their maintenance planning activities.' Scope layers include a LiDAR point cloud as the twin foundation, asset data for linear and non-linear assets, and - verbatim - 'Fault Notifications and work orders'. The closest published analogue to this repo's PdM/CDT use case. Collected use case of the JTC 1/AG 11 report (Annex B), documented with the Annex A template.

cross_references.series: Companion of ISO/IEC 30173 (concepts and terminology; several terms sourced from it as ISO/IEC 30173:-). Use cases collected from the JTC 1/AG 11 report.
cross_references.pdm_anchor: B.11 (Sydney Trains Engineering and Maintenance Digital Twin) is the closest published analogue to this repo's use case: an asset digital twin for rail maintenance layering asset data, fault notifications and work orders - the same spine this KG formalizes. The conformity term (3.6) names the CDT-readiness judgement the checker renders.
